name: Forillon National Park
reservation: National Park entry fees are required and can be paid at the interpretation centers at the L'Anse-au-Griffon or Penouille entrances. Camping reservations for stays at Des-Rosiers or Petit-Gaspé must be made through the Parks Canada national system well in advance. Entry for day use does not currently require a prior reservation, but peak weekends can see crowded parking lots.

days.title: Land's End and Maritime History

stops.name: Cap-Bon-Ami
stops.detail: View the dramatic vertical limestone cliffs and watch for nesting seabirds from the lookout platforms.

stops.name: Mont-Saint-Alban Tower
stops.detail: Hike to the observation tower for a 360-degree view of the Gulf of St. Lawrence and the interior Appalachian mountains.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from Gaspé to the park entrance; conditions vary.
days.note: The hike to the tower is steep; allow ample time for the ascent and descent.

days.title: Heritage of the Peninsula
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the South Sector

stops.name: Grande-Grave Heritage Site
stops.detail: Explore the preserved 19th-century fishing village buildings, including the general store and Hyman House.

stops.name: Cap-Gaspé Lighthouse
stops.detail: Walk the 'Les Parages' trail to the end of the Gaspé Peninsula where the lighthouse overlooks the ship channel.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local shuttle or driving between sectors; conditions vary.
days.note: Whales are frequently visible from the cliffs near Cap-Gaspé during the summer months.

days.title: Coastal Lowlands and Salt Marshes

stops.name: Penouille Beach
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalks through the salt marsh and taiga, a unique ecosystem at this latitude.

stops.name: Fort Peninsula
stops.detail: Visit the only partially preserved World War II coastal battery in Quebec, once used to guard the Bay of Gaspé.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for transit between the Penouille and Fort sectors; conditions vary.
days.note: The Penouille area is ideal for cycling; bike rentals are often available near the visitor center.

intel.title: Cap-Bon-Ami Capacity
intel.text: The parking area at Cap-Bon-Ami is relatively small and often reaches capacity by midday in August. Consider visiting early in the morning or late afternoon to secure a spot.

intel.title: Topographic Interference
intel.text: Reception is strong near the town of Gaspé but becomes intermittent in the deep valleys of the park's North Sector. Download topographic maps for inland hiking trails.

intel.title: Gaspé and Riviere-au-Renard
intel.text: Fuel stations are located in the towns flanking the park. There are no fuel services within the park boundaries, so fill up before entering the South or North sectors.

intel.title: Wildlife Awareness
intel.text: Black bears are common in Forillon; park staff may close specific trails if bear activity is high. Check the notice boards at visitor centers for daily updates.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: The scenic park roads are generally open from June to October. Outside this window, services are closed and most roads are not plowed for vehicle access.

plan.arrival: Fly into Michel-Pouliot Gaspé Airport and rent a car; pick up all major grocery supplies in the town of Gaspé before proceeding to the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for the main loops, but ensure your rental allows for driving on secondary gravel access roads if visiting remote trailheads.
plan.goldenHour: Cap-Bon-Ami for sunrise, as the cliffs catch the first light over the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
